correction_1_decision_logic_reclassifica.topic: Reclassification of Decision Logic Case from CASE C to CASE B
correction_1_decision_logic_reclassifica.previous_status: CASE C (Primary metric interpretation is materially distorted by rare-support structure and single-parent vulnerability)
correction_1_decision_logic_reclassifica.corrected_status: CASE B (The frozen primary metric remains valid for its intended macro-class objective, but its estimate is materially sensitive to uneven physical support and sparse class representation in the current DEV partition)
correction_1_decision_logic_reclassifica.normative_calibration_rationale: Equal class weighting is an intentional, standard property of macro arithmetic mIoU. When rare classes score low, the headline macro score is naturally lower than a pixel-weighted descriptive summary. Without an external normative requirement specifying that macro mIoU must mirror pixel-weighted prevalence, the metric is support-sensitive, not mathematically invalid or distorted.

correction_2_evaluation_subset_sensitivi.topic: Descriptive Evaluation-Subset Sensitivity vs Artificial Mathematical Boost
correction_2_evaluation_subset_sensitivi.previous_phrasing: Single-parent classes produce an artificial mathematical boost (+0.004 to +0.0105) and acute instability
correction_2_evaluation_subset_sensitivi.corrected_phrasing: Descriptive evaluation-subset sensitivity: when the sole parent containing a class is omitted, that class has 0 GT pixels in the remaining subset. Under the frozen metric rules, classes with 0 GT pixels are legitimately excluded from the macro denominator (reducing it from 11 to 10), resulting in a subset score that is higher (+0.004 to +0.0105) over fewer classes. This is not an artificial boost or defect in the full-DEV benchmark.

correction_3_equal_class_weighting.previous_phrasing: Ultra-sparse and intermediate classes mechanically compress the apparent macro performance from 0.119 to 0.049
correction_3_equal_class_weighting.corrected_phrasing: Equal class-weighting and support sensitivity: each class contributes equally (1/11th) regardless of pixel footprint. Low-IoU classes contribute equally at the class level despite smaller pixel support, so the headline macro score is lower than a pixel-weighted summary. The ~0.049 score is a valid macro-class performance measure with substantial support sensitivity.

authoritative_diagnostic_roadmap.core_question: Did pseudo-random batch sampling schedules starve rare classes of gradient exposure during the critical initial epochs (Epochs 1-7) prior to early stopping?
